watches.name: Cereal - Marshmallow Magic (Rampart Studio X Doug Bloodworth)
watches.description: Saturday mornings, now on your wrist. watches.name: Blackout - Printing & Offset Crown
watches.description: At one time, the US-based Hamilton Watch Company stood at the center of horological excellence. At its heart was the 921caliber, an impeccably accurate pocket watch movement built with meticulous decoration and finishing. But time changes value. As gold prices rose, countless pocket watch cases were melted for scrap. What remained: The movements. The dials. On some, solid gold components, including a gold center wheel and 10 to 14K gold numerals. The 921’s accuracy, beauty, and proportions make it ideal for resurrection. Slim enough to become a wristwatch. We fully restore each movement. Then regulate it to perform at its original factory tolerances, or better. Then: Each dial is stripped to bare metal. Refinished in deep, unforgiving black. The hands and numerals are polished. Tracks are reprinted. The result: Gold against dark. Modern, bold, unmistakable. This isn’t a restoration. It’s a reawakening. Housed in a 45mm precision-machined 316L stainless steel case. 12mm thin. Sapphire crystal. Exhibition caseback. Built to be worn, not archived. This is Blackout. By Rampart Studio. Specs: Case: 44mm 316L Steel Glass: Sapphire front and sapphire exhibition case back Movement: Fully Restored Hamilton 921, beautiful finishing with solid gold centerwheel. Dial: Designed, painted, pad printed, and fabricated in house in the United States Strap: Lightly padded high grade leather, black. *Center wheels and numerals known to be 10K or 14k solid gold, though untested.

watches.description: Rare, Vintage Hamilton Wristwatch Case: 14k gold-filled, finished with a precision-applied Cerakote ceramic coating—ultra-thin, exceptionally durable, and engineered to elevate performance and presence. Dial: In-house fabricated in purple, stamped "Blasphemy" Movement: Hamilton Made in USA Era: Circa 1940s Fully restored. One of one. Is this watchmaking blasphemy ? Vintage American wristwatches don’t get restored. They decay. Beautifully built and decorated movements fade into obscurity. Cases, once high-quality gold-fill: they carry the marks of a century of wear. Not character. Neglect. We start where others stop. We’re buying vintage American timepieces before they disappear forever. We fully restore the movements: cleaned, rebuilt, and regulated beyond factory spec. Then we change the look. Completely. We treat original gold-fill cases with an ultra-thin, highly durable ceramic Cerakote finish: a modern coating engineered for exceptional adhesion, corrosion resistance, and long-term stability. Remarkably tough. Surprisingly refined. The result is protection without bulk. Longevity without compromise. A bold, contemporary surface that lets these watches live another century on the wrist—not in a drawer. Then, we sand the dials back to raw brass and refinish them in bold, unexpected colors. We pair them with equally bold, top-tier leather straps. New crystals. Polished cases. Refinished hands and markers. It’s an extraordinary amount of work re-imagining forgotten American masterpieces into something new, modern, wearable, and alive again. Some purists will hate it. So, we’ll ask you: Are we committing blasphemy? Or preventing it?

watches.name: Fauxgraph - Silver, Charcoal
watches.description: *Hot Months: Fauxgraph Ships with Three Bracelets: Leather, Silicone, & Steel Micro Mesh The chronograph is one of watchmaking’s great icons. Also, almost nobody uses the complication. The Fauxgraph is built around that uncomfortable reality . It borrows the visual language of the chronograph, and removes the rest. No pushers. No timing scale. No complication you feel faintly guilty for not using or needing. What remains is pure composition : an unmistakable chronograph presence, stripped of everything performative except the performance itself . The dial is pad printed in-house at our U.S.-based studio. Inside is a genuine top-grade ETA 2892 , one of the great thin automatic movements, at its highest grade for finish and performance. The case comes from the Ickler family in Germany, a generational case maker known for precision manufacturing and exceptional finishing. The strap is custom made in the United States. Quantities obscenely limited. watches.name: American Anthem
watches.description: For America’s 250th, Rampart Studio created a dial that is part portrait, part poster, part noise. Abraham Lincoln appears with an electric guitar against a field of saturated color, texture, and distortion — a deliberately unexpected image of an American icon. The dial was designed and printed in-house using UV printing, giving it depth, texture, and deep color. The watch is built around a 39mm 316L steel case by Ickler, measuring just 9.5mm thin, with a sapphire crystal and exhibition caseback displaying a Top Grade ETA 2892-A2 automatic movement. The strap is U.S.-made full-grain matte leather: unpadded, tapered, and finished with a with a bold green stitching and brushed rivets. American Anthem is Rampart Studio’s tribute to 250 years of the United States: independent, loud, and unmistakably original. Specs Case: 39mm 316L precision steel by Ickler Thickness: 9.5mm Lug to lug: 45.4mm Crystal: Sapphire front and exhibition caseback Date: Window at 3 O’clock Dial: In-house designed and UV printed Movement: Top Grade ETA 2892-A2 automatic (highest finishing level) Power reserve: 42 hours Frequency: 28,800 vph Water resistance: 5 ATM Strap: Custom U.S.-made full-grain matte leather with green stitching and brushed rivets

Beautifully built and decorated movements fade into obscurity. Cases, once high-quality gold-fill: they carry the marks of a century of wear. Not character. Neglect. We start where others stop. We’re buying vintage American timepieces before they disappear forever. We fully restore the movements: cleaned, rebuilt, and regulated beyond factory spec. Then we change the look. Completely. We treat original gold-fill cases with an ultra-thin, highly durable ceramic Cerakote finish: a modern coating engineered for exceptional adhesion, corrosion resistance, and long-term stability. Remarkably tough. Surprisingly refined. The result is protection without bulk. Longevity without compromise. A bold, contemporary surface that lets these watches live another century on the wrist—not in a drawer. Then, we sand the dials back to raw brass and refinish them in bold, unexpected colors. We pair them with equally bold, top-tier leather straps. New crystals. Polished cases. Refinished hands and markers. It’s an extraordinary amount of work re-imagining forgotten American masterpieces into something new, modern, wearable, and alive again. Some purists will hate it. So, we’ll ask you: Are we committing blasphemy? Or preventing it?
